words.gloss: he who has an envious heart

literal: The prosperity of the envious-hearted person and the ruin of the upright person will be pondered.
translation: The prosperity of an envious-hearted person and the adversity of an upright person are matters to be deeply pondered.
modern: பொறாமை குணம் கொண்டவனுடைய செல்வமும், நேர்மையானவனுடைய வறுமையும் (மக்களால் வியப்புடன்) ஆராய்ந்து நினைக்கப்படும்.
explanation: This couplet addresses a common paradox in human life: the prosperity of the wicked and the suffering of the righteous. The poet states that the wealth of an envious person (அவ்விய நெஞ்சத்தான் ஆக்கம்) and the ruin of an upright person (செவ்வியான் கேடு) are anomalies that will be deeply pondered and analyzed by the world. Here, 'அவ்வியம்' refers to envy or crookedness of the mind, while 'செவ்வி' refers to rectitude or equity. By stating that these situations are 'to be pondered' (நினைக்கப்படும்), the poet implies that such unnatural states of fortune are temporary, unnatural, and bound to be resolved by the laws of nature.
